_README: Keys starting with _ are notes and are ignored by the code. Values marked ASSUMPTION have no public source yet: say so on the card and test them in 'sensitivity'.

_downloads.1_acs: Needs a free Census API key (https://api.census.gov/data/key_signup.html); in Terminal run  export CENSUS_KEY=your_key  first. Then: curl -o raw/acs_s1810.json "https://api.census.gov/data/2024/acs/acs5/subject?get=NAME,S1810_C01_001E,S1810_C02_047E&for=tract:*&in=state:36%20county:005&key=$CENSUS_KEY"  (county 005 = Bronx; 047 Brooklyn, 061 Manhattan, 081 Queens, 085 Staten Island). Before freezing, confirm the label at https://api.census.gov/data/2024/acs/acs5/subject/variables/S1810_C02_047E.html reads 'Estimate!!With a disability!!...!!With an ambulatory difficulty'. If 2024 fails, use 2023 in both URLs.
_downloads.3_facilities: NYC Facilities Database (FacDB) CSV from NYC Planning (Bytes of the Big Apple) or NYC Open Data; save as raw/facilities.csv
_downloads.5_blocks: Save (keep zipped) as raw/tl_2020_36_tabblock20.zip: https://www2.census.gov/geo/tiger/TIGER2020/TABBLOCK20/tl_2020_36_tabblock20.zip  (2020 Census blocks for New York State, with population POP20 and internal points; about 100+ MB). Needs: pip3 install pyshp
_downloads.4_registrants: MTA NYCT Paratransit Registrants: Beginning 2018 -> Export -> CSV, from https://data.ny.gov/d/cxps-6wkq ; save as raw/registrants.csv

service_area: Bronx, all census tracts with ambulatory-difficulty population (ACS)
_home_location: SOURCE: homes are placed at populated 2020 Census blocks (TIGER/Line TABBLOCK20, POP20 > 0) inside the ACS-weighted tract, chosen by block population, at the Census block internal point. No random scatter, so no homes in water, parks or unpopulated land.
_destination_factype_weights: ASSUMPTION (weights): exact NYC Facilities Database facility types (factype) -> relative share of trips. Hospitals 5; diagnostic & treatment centers and adult day programs 3; extension clinics, senior centers and programs for people with disabilities 2; general senior services and mental-health clinics 1. Every other type is excluded, including school-based, mobile and child health clinics, programs for students with disabilities, housing (enriched housing, NORCs) and office-type services (case management, legal, meals, caregiver, NY Connects). FacDB has no separate dialysis type: NY licenses dialysis centers as diagnostic & treatment centers or their extension clinics, so they are picked out by name (dialysis_name_keywords) and weighted like hospitals.
_dialysis: ASSUMPTION (weight): any listed health facility whose name contains one of these words is treated as a dialysis center and weighted 5, because dialysis patients ride about three times a week. Check data/dialysis_found.csv against a map or the CMS Dialysis Facility listing.
_trips_in_area_peak: null = computed as weekday_trips_citywide x borough share of registrants x peak share
_weekday_trips_citywide: SOURCE: MTA Board Update, Access-A-Ride, June 25 2025 (mta.info/document/177266): '40,000+ scheduled weekday trips'. Can be updated from MTA NYCT Paratransit Ridership: Beginning 2024 (data.ny.gov hasd-hdb7).
_borough_registrant_share: null = read from data/derived.json (MTA Paratransit Registrants by borough, latest month)
_peak_share_of_daily_trips: ASSUMPTION: share of weekday trips requested 7:00-10:00. No public hourly AAR data found; tested in sensitivity.
_outbound_share: ASSUMPTION: share of AM-peak trips going home -> destination
_wheelchair_share: SOURCE: NYS Comptroller, MTA's Paratransit Program: An Overview (Report 12-2024, Nov 2023), p.3: wheelchair users are 16% of Bronx registrants (15% citywide). Registrants, not trips.
_speed: ASSUMPTION. Check: the run prints mean solo ride time. MTA paratransit reports in NYCT committee books show average actual trip duration of roughly 34-40 min, which includes today's shared detours, so solo rides should come out somewhat below that.
_dwell: ASSUMPTION: boarding/alighting minutes; replace with carrier interview or field-observation numbers
_window_min: SOURCE: AAR's promise. Riders are told to be ready at the scheduled pickup time and to wait up to 30 minutes after it (MTA, Access-A-Ride 'Take a trip' and Customer Bill of Rights). So a pickup-time trip must be picked up 0 to +30 min after its requested time, never early. AAR's on-time metric uses 20 min (MTA Pickup On-Time Performance dataset): tested in window_20. The card's original +/-15 is tested in hypothesis_pm15.
_appointment_share_outbound: ASSUMPTION: share of outbound (home -> destination) trips booked by appointment time instead of pickup time. AAR lets riders book either. Tested at 0.5 and 0.
_appt: SOURCE: MTA NYCT Paratransit Drop-off On-Time Performance (data.ny.gov): an appointment trip is on time if it arrives no more than 30 minutes early and no later than the appointment time.
_max_ride_table: SOURCE: AAR Maximum Ride Times by trip distance (MTA, Access-A-Ride 'Take a trip' page): 0-<3 mi 50 min; 3-<6 mi 65; 6-<9 mi 95; 9-<12 mi 115; 12-<14 mi 135; 14+ mi 155. Each entry is [upper mile limit, minutes]. Trip miles = straight-line distance x circuity.
_max_ride_buffer: ASSUMPTION: pooled rides are planned to use at most this share of AAR's maximum ride time, leaving slack for traffic, late riders and slow boarding (a plan has none of these). 0.9 = at most 45 of the 50 minutes allowed for a trip under 3 miles. AAR reports about 99% of trips within max ride time, not 100%. Tested at 1.0 (no buffer) and 0.8.
_ride_caps: Optional extra caps on top of AAR's table (null = off). The added_20_cap / added_10_cap scenarios test stricter rider-experience limits.
_prefilter_time_min: Technical: two trips whose estimated pickups are more than this many minutes apart are never tested together. Set wide enough not to exclude feasible groups.
_vehicle: ASSUMPTION: one dedicated lift-equipped van type (MTA reports 1,150 such vehicles; seat layout not published). Replace with fleet research. The broker_sedan scenario tests sedans, which carry no wheelchairs.
_solver: Assignment is solved to within solver_gap of optimal or until the time limit; summary.csv records the gap actually reached.
_baseline_note: SOURCE: NYS Comptroller Report 12-2024, p.3: 75% of AAR trips are not shared today; broker (mostly sedan/for-hire) trips were 62.6% of trips and primary-carrier vans 23.2% in April 2023 (p.4). The control here is 'all solo', so report results against that 75% figure too.
_seeds: Base runs all 20 seeds; each sensitivity scenario runs the first 5 (looser limits are much slower). Same seed = same trips, as long as the scenario doesn't change trip generation (peak_share scenarios do).
